coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Rock Channel Wharf

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE but high confidence: all four edges are recorded DataSF lot lines (the notch of lot 8719A003), agreeing with the Design Controls figures to within a few metres. Planned open space. The Design Controls (April 24, 2018, Section 3.5) describe Channel Wharf as continuing 'to serve as a functioning wharf while providing public access'; what occupies the notch today has not been checked against a current source.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor lot lines: the notch of the Terry A Francois Boulevard lot 8719A003 east of the roadway, between the Pier 48 lot 8719A001 and Pier 50; cross-checked against Mission Rock Design Controls Figure 1.1 (p.10), Figure 3.1.1 (p.45) and Section 3.5 (p.68).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The wharf is part of the Terry A Francois Boulevard right-of-way lot 8719A003 (DataSF Assessor parcels, recorded 2020-06-12), which also carries the roadway and its paseo; joining status.csv to that lot would paint the whole boulevard (our mapping rationale, not a statement of the Design Controls).
notes.regulatory_context: Dedicated open space, Design Controls Section 3.5: a paved working-wharf plaza with public access, seating, a large-scale industrial feature, consistent with Public Trust uses; reached from Channel Lane across TAFB.

milestones.text: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock Design Controls, which name this planned open space as Channel Wharf (Design Controls Section 3.5); the Port's Jan 26, 2018 staff report requested this approval under Resolution 18-04, and its Sept 2019 memo dates the Commission's approvals January 30, 2018 (it numbers the Design Controls resolution 18-05)

sources.title: Port Commission Item 11A staff report, Jan 26 2018 (request); Port Commission Item 7A memo, Sept 20 2019 (approval date)

milestones.source: Port Commission Item 11A staff report, Jan 26 2018 (request); Port Commission Item 7A memo, Sept 20 2019 (approval date)

changes.text: The map notes said the wharf is unbuilt and a working wharf or staging area today, and cited the Design Controls for the boulevard lot 8719A003. A 2018 plan cannot show today's condition: the notes now quote what the Design Controls say (Channel Wharf continues to serve as a functioning wharf while providing public access), cite the Port's June 2026 report, and say the current condition is not confirmed. The lot facts now cite DataSF's Assessor parcels. The Jan 30, 2018 Design Controls approval milestone and its change entry now cite the Sept 2019 Port memo that states the date.

record.notes: Planned waterfront plaza between Piers 48 and 50 (Design Controls Section 3.5). No source read reports it built: the Port's June 5, 2026 report lists China Basin Park among Phase 1's deliveries and mentions the marginal wharf only as part of the project site. Its current condition is not confirmed.
